findings.text: the diff edits tests/test_domain_rules_reach_the_brief.py, which is outside the node's declared exclusive write paths; the node discloses it in its manifest's blockers line as an authorisation request rather than hiding it, and the edit is required because those three call sites named the composer the plan deletes, so reverting it would restore a red declared gate. The coordinator must authorise the scope expansion or own the file in a separate node.

assert first == second compares two calls of the deterministic _brief_digest over the same unchanged brief path, so it holds whatever the code does and cannot fail; the done_when clause 'the brief digest of an unchanged node is unchanged' therefore has no guard behind it. An independent assertion would pin the digest to a value derived from the fixture's own bytes rather than to a second call of the same function.

assert rendered == "\n".join([DOMAIN_RULES_HEADING, render_review_check(check)]) derives both sides from the same code under test with the same test-supplied check, so a regression of render_review_check itself (for example returning a line without the id) changes both sides identically and the assertion still passes; it guards only the case where render_domain_rules stops routing through the helper, and is not evidence that the helper renders a check correctly.
